notes: Round 5: continued fine-tuning round 4's model on the same merged dataset using categorical focal loss (gamma=2.0) instead of plain cross-entropy -- focal loss down-weights already-easy examples and concentrates gradient on hard ones, a different mechanism than class-weighting (tried previously, no effect). Glioma recall rose from 0.89 to 0.90 (9 fewer misclassifications: 590/654 vs 581/654), pituitary reached near-perfect F1. A prior full-model ensemble (2 independently-trained models averaged) had shown 0% improvement over the single model and confirmed 0.89 recall as a reproducible ceiling for plain cross-entropy training on this data -- focal loss modestly moved past that ceiling. Two known hard real-world images (used as ongoing spot-checks, not part of training or the formal test set) remain misclassified as meningioma, consistent with the fact that even at 90% recall roughly 1 in 10 real glioma cases is still missed.
